equation_request.abstract:
We show that the depth of quantum circuits in the realistic architecture where a classical controller determines which local interactions to apply on the kD grid Zk where k ≥ 2 is the same (up to a constant factor) as in the standard model where arbitrary interactions are allowed. This allows minimum-depth circuits (up to a constant factor) for the nearest-neighbor architecture to be obtained from minimum-depth circuits in the standard abstract model. Our work therefore justifies the standard assumption that interactions can be performed between arbitrary pairs of qubits. In particular, our results imply that Shor's algorithm, controlled operations and fanouts can be implemented in constant depth, polynomial size and polynomial width in this architecture.

We also present optimal non-adaptive quantum circuits for controlled operations and fanouts on a kD grid. These circuits have depth Θ( k√n), size Θ(n) and width Θ(n). Our lower bound also applies to a more general class of operations.

specification.problem: Show how a classically controlled (adaptive) circuit on a kD nearest-neighbor grid can simulate an abstract-depth-d circuit with arbitrary pairwise gates in O(d) depth. The tiny scoped instance is a nonlocal CNOT between two logical qubits that sit at distant sites on a 1D line segment of the grid. The line is used as a stand-in routing path, which is the smallest case of the grid path routing. The gate is implemented by constant-depth entanglement swapping, gate teleportation and classical Pauli feed-forward.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Only the following is reconstructed: (a) a constant-depth Bell pair between the endpoints of a path of m+1 qubits via parallel Bell measurements and an XOR Pauli correction; (b) a nonlocal CNOT via that Bell pair, as local CNOTs, measurements and Pauli fixes; (c) the non-adaptive fanout lightcone bound as a counting statement. Outside this scope: full layer-by-layer routing and congestion resolution in k>=2 dimensions, Pauli-frame absorption by Clifford conjugation, the constant-depth Shor circuit, GHZ/fanout in constant depth, and the optimal Theta(n^(1/k)) non-adaptive construction in full.

symbols.domain: integer, k>=2 in the paper; k=1 line used for the tiny instance

symbols.meaning: number of logical qubits or fanout targets
number of Bell-pair links along a routing path
outcome bit of the j-th Bell measurement (X-parity bit x_j, Z-parity bit z_j)
swap measurement outcomes at the j-th intermediate site

equations.label: Bell pair
equations.description: Short-range Bell pair preparation in constant depth, used for each link of the path.
assumptions: Neighboring sites can interact via CNOT

equations.label: Entanglement swapping correction
equations.latex: \bigotimes_{j=1}^{m-1}(\text{Bell meas. on pair }j)\;:\;|\Phi^+\rangle^{\otimes m}\to (X^{\oplus_j x_j}Z^{\oplus_j z_j}\otimes I)|\Phi^+\rangle_{\text{ends}}
equations.description: All intermediate Bell measurements run in parallel; the end pair is Bell up to a Pauli whose exponents are the XOR of outcomes, computed classically. Depth is constant independent of m.
equations.abstract_quote: classical controller determines which local interactions to apply
equations.justification: Standard entanglement swapping combined with the sketch's parallel-path claim; the abstract only claims constant-depth simulation with classical control.
assumptions: Mid-circuit measurement and feed-forward cost zero depth

equations.label: Nonlocal CNOT via Bell pair
equations.latex: \mathrm{CNOT}_{a\to b}:\ \text{CNOT}_{a\to e_a},\ \text{measure }e_a\to u;\ X^{u}\text{ on }e_b;\ \text{CNOT}_{e_b\to b};\ H\text{ on }e_b,\text{ measure}\to v;\ Z^{v}\text{ on }a
equations.description: Standard gate teleportation of a CNOT using Bell pair halves e_a, e_b (a is the control, b is the target). Outcomes u,v drive the fixes. The ends e_a, e_b are first Pauli-corrected from eq_2.
equations.justification: Textbook nonlocal CNOT with one ebit; the paper's exact protocol is not given.
assumptions: Bell pair is exact after correction

equations.label: Fanout lightcone bound
equations.description: A non-adaptive fanout from one control to n targets needs depth at least about n^(1/k) because the number of grid sites in the lightcone grows as O(t^k).
equations.abstract_quote: These circuits have depth Θ( k√n), size Θ(n) and width Θ(n).
equations.justification: Reading the abstract's k-th root of n as n^(1/k) and the lightcone argument from the sketch.
assumptions: c is a constant depending on k

equations.label: Fanout action
equations.description: Fanout is one control with n CNOT targets, so size Theta(n) with one CNOT per target.

registers.name: logical
registers.size: 2 (control a and target b for the tiny instance)

registers.name: path
registers.size: 2m (m links, 2 qubits each; the endpoints e_a and e_b are among them)

registers.name: classical
registers.role: swap outcomes plus gate-teleportation outcomes u,v

specification.initial_state: Logical qubits in an arbitrary test state (e.g. |+>|0> to give a Bell pair after the CNOT); all ancillas in |0>.

steps.description: Prepare m Bell pairs on adjacent ancilla pairs along the path, in constant depth.
Perform parallel Bell measurements on the adjacent middle qubits, XOR the outcomes classically, and apply the resulting Pauli to one end (or track it in the frame).
Apply the teleported CNOT from a to b using the end qubits, with measurements and feed-forward fixes.
Verify that the output equals the ideal CNOT; for fanout, compare with the ideal action and check the n^(1/k) depth scaling.

specification.measurement: Mid-circuit Bell measurements on the intermediate qubits and the gate-teleportation measurements. Final check: the statevector or counts of the logical register after the corrections. Qiskit is little-endian: bit i is set by measure(i,i) and is the last character in counts keys.
specification.classical_postprocessing: XOR the swap outcomes to get the Pauli on the end pair, then compute the u,v fixes. The Pauli frame can be applied by classically conditioned gates or tracked.
assumptions: Tiny instance chosen: nonlocal CNOT over a 1D path with m=2 or 3, as an illustration
Mid-circuit measurement and feed-forward are free in depth
The controller computes the routing and corrections for free
Depth is counted over quantum layers only
